correctness.rationale: The two-step killed walk has b=2 sole even state, giving s_t=(pq)^t. At b=3 a 2×2 substochastic kernel has s_t=p(2pq)^(t−1) for t>=1, so first hazard comparison requires p>=1/2. At b=4 its two eigenvalues ((3±sqrt5)/2)pq yield s_t=A λ+^t+B λ−^t with A>0 and log-concavity determinant −AB(λ+−λ−)^2(λ+λ−)^(t−1). This is >=0 exactly when p >=(sqrt5−1)/2, with equality all ages at the boundary. For b>=5, no upper absorption in four steps and exact Catalan-prefix enumeration gives s1=p and s2=p²(2−p), hence h2−h1=−p(1−p)<0. At b=1 absorption first step. Independent exact fractions checked b<=8 and five biases; analytic arguments handle all 0<p<1, all b.
